“They saw no one, except Jesus alone”
(Matthew 17:8)
Key points:
1. Open with the key verse, then ask: this past week, what picture has filled your heart most often — Jesus, or yourself?
2. Give the title and subtitle: when our focus turns to ourselves, fear swallows up faith.
3. The key verse comes from the end of the Transfiguration (Matthew 17:8).
4. Preview the four stretches of road: Eden, the Sea of Galilee, the wilderness of Kadesh, the Lord’s prayer for unity.

brief12.title: Introduction: The Glance That Brings Us Down
notes: Slide text:
Only one-ninth of an iceberg shows
What tore the hull lay beneath
What sinks us is not the storm
but our gaze fixed on ourselves
Key points:
1. The Titanic struck an iceberg in 1912; about one-ninth of an iceberg floats above the water (sea ice about 920, seawater about 1,025 kg per cubic metre).
2. Application: what tore the hull was below the surface; what sinks a Christian is “looking at self”.
3. Describe how fear seeps in: prayer grows heavy, fellowship becomes a chore, we dare not speak in the group chat.
4. Lead into Genesis 3: the first thing humans felt was not repentance but fear.

brief12.title: Key Verse and Background
notes: Slide text:
“Lifting up their eyes, they saw no one,
except Jesus alone.”
(Matthew 17:8)
The Transfiguration: the Father says, Listen to him
Key points:
1. Background: the author, Matthew, was Levi the tax collector; written around AD 50–70 for Jewish believers.
2. Context: Peter confessed “You are the Christ” (Matthew 16:16), then was rebuked at once for “setting his mind on the things of men” (Matthew 16:23).
3. The Transfiguration is a lesson in training the eyes; Peter wanted three tents, and the Father said, “This is my beloved Son … Listen to him” (Matthew 17:5).
4. From the original: the “alone” in “Jesus alone” is μόνον.

brief12.title: 1. When the Focus Turns to Self
notes: Slide text:
Eyes opened — and the first thing seen was self
Fear is reverence aimed at the wrong object
Cover, hide, shift the blame
(Genesis 3:7–10)
Key points:
1. Read Genesis 3:7–10: the first appearance of “afraid” in the Bible.
2. Wordplay in the original: “naked”, arummim (Genesis 2:25), sounds almost like the serpent’s “subtle”, arum (Genesis 3:1).
3. “Afraid”, yare’, can also mean reverent fear; fear is reverence aimed at the wrong object.
4. Psychology: Nolen-Hoeksema’s research at Yale on “rumination” — staring at yourself only deepens depression.
5. 321: the old self is self-centred, the new self is selfless; pride is leaving our originally intended position to take God’s place, humility is returning to it.

brief12.title: 2. Seeing Self, We Cannot See Jesus
notes: Slide text:
See our lack — can’t believe his abundance
See our smallness — can’t rely on his greatness
See our weakness — can’t know his power
(Matthew 14:28–30)
Key points:
1. Read Matthew 14:28–30.
2. Three parallel lines: seeing our lack / smallness / weakness, we cannot believe in the Lord’s abundance / greatness / almighty power.
3. Reminder: of the twelve, only Peter got out of the boat — don’t look down on him; the problem was the focus.
4. Focus on self = self-pity, self-blame, anxiety and fear.

brief12.title: Why Peter Sank
notes: Slide text:
“When he saw that the wind was strong, he was afraid”
The wind didn’t change; his eyes did
Looking to Jesus: eyes taken off everything else
One look at self, ten looks at Christ
Key points:
1. Key word: “saw” is βλέπων, a continuing gaze; the wind was there all along — what changed was his eyes.
2. Compare Hebrews 12:2, “looking to”: ἀφορῶντες = taking the eyes off everything else.
3. Harvard gorilla experiment (Simons and Chabris, 1999, Perception): about half never saw the gorilla.
4. Quote: M’Cheyne is generally credited with saying, “For every look at yourself, take ten looks at Christ.”
5. The Lord “immediately stretched out his hand” (Matthew 14:31); his hand is faster than our failure.

brief12.title: 3. Faith or Fear: Walk by Only One
notes: Slide text:
“We were in our own sight as grasshoppers”
(Numbers 13:33)
“Don’t be afraid. Don’t be dismayed”
(Joshua 1:9)
Key points:
1. The twelve spies at Kadesh; their report was accurate but then turned (Numbers 13:27–28).
2. Verse wording: read the full verse as given in the Bible text, “We were in our own sight as grasshoppers” (Numbers 13:33).
3. “In their sight” was a projection out of thin air; Rahab later said, “As soon as we had heard it, our hearts melted” (Joshua 2:11).
4. Verse wording: for “Don’t be afraid … I am with you”, read the full verse, Joshua 1:9.
5. Psychology: Kahneman and Tversky’s 1979 Prospect Theory — a loss hurts about twice as much as an equal gain pleases.

brief12.title: 4. Separation Makes Us See Too Much of Self
notes: Slide text:
When do we notice a drop of water?
When it is alone, separated
Small drops evaporate; rivers don’t run dry
In unity: not self, but Jesus alone
Key points:
1. Open with a question: when do you notice a single drop of water?
2. Science: the larger the ratio of surface area to volume, the faster water evaporates; isolation exposes us, gathering preserves us.
3. Theology: “It is not good for the man to be alone” (Genesis 2:18) was said before the Fall.
4. Data: Holt-Lunstad’s 2010 meta-analysis at Brigham Young University — 148 studies, over 300,000 people; strong social connections raised the likelihood of survival by about 50%.
5. Scripture: Ecclesiastes 4:9–12; John 7:38, rivers of living water.

brief12.title: 321: From Self-Centred to Selfless
notes: Slide text:
The old self is self-centred; the new self is selfless
Humility overcomes pride
Selflessness overcomes Satan
The focus is Jesus, not ourselves
Key points:
1. Sum up: all four points come down to one thing — focus.
2. The old self is self-centred, the new self is selfless; selflessness is not having nothing but entering the limitless.
3. All three times Satan tempted the Lord he said, “If you are the Son of God”, trying to shift the focus from the Father to self.
4. Pride stirs up pride, and both sides lose; humility draws out humility, and both sides win.
5. 920: everyone we relate to is a “2”; living out the “0” bears the ninefold fruit of the Spirit (Galatians 5:22–23).

brief12.title: Putting It into Practice
notes: Slide text:
Notice when you start looking at yourself
Replace fear with the language of faith
Reach out and connect; refuse isolation
Reminder: let truth be greater than feelings
Key points:
1. Practice 1: notice the three “looking at self” sentences and say at once, “Lord Jesus, I turn to you.”
2. Luther is generally credited with saying: you can’t stop birds flying over your head, but you can stop them building a nest.
3. Practice 2: three declarations of faith, backed by 2 Corinthians 12:9, Isaiah 41:10 and Matthew 19:26.
4. Practice 3: greet a member of the body, share a struggle, join a small group (James 5:16: confess to one another, pray for one another).
5. Gentle reminder: feelings are good servants but bad masters; let truth be greater than feelings (Psalm 12:6).

brief12.title: Closing and Call
notes: Slide text:
“Not a spirit of fear, but of power,
love, and self-control”
(2 Timothy 1:7)
Lift your head out of fear and see Jesus
Key points:
1. Verse wording: read the full verse, 2 Timothy 1:7 (“power, love, and self-control”).
2. The original: fear δειλία, power δύναμις, love ἀγάπη, self-control σωφρονισμός.
3. Paul wrote this least fearful of sentences in a Roman prison.
4. Back to the scene: the Lord came, touched them and said, “Get up, and don’t be afraid” (Matthew 17:7).
5. Call: let Jesus be King; let Jesus receive all the glory.

brief12.title: Response Prayer and Blessing
notes: Slide text:
Lord, I will no longer look at myself
I will fix my eyes on you
May I lift my eyes and see no one
except Jesus alone
Key points:
1. Lead the congregation in reading the declaration of faith together: Lord, I will no longer look at myself; I will fix my eyes on you.
2. Prayer points: forgive us for a misplaced focus; Lord, reach out and touch me; Holy Spirit, help me turn; Lord, lead me into unity.
3. Remind them of this week’s three practices and encourage them to follow up with one another.
4. Blessing: may the brothers and sisters, when they lift their eyes, see no one except Jesus alone.

brief21.title: Seeing Self Brings Fear
notes: Slide text:
When our focus turns to ourselves,
fear swallows up faith
“They saw no one, except Jesus alone”
(Matthew 17:8)
Key points:
1. Greet everyone, then ask: this past week, what picture has filled your heart most often — Jesus, or yourself?
2. Announce the title and subtitle: when our focus turns to ourselves, fear swallows up faith.
3. The key verse is the end of the Transfiguration (Matthew 17:8).
4. Preview the four stretches of road: Eden, the Sea of Galilee, the wilderness of Kadesh, the Lord’s prayer for unity.

brief21.title: Introduction: The Mass Beneath the Surface
notes: Slide text:
About one-ninth of an iceberg shows
What tore the Titanic lay beneath
What really sinks us is not the storm
but the unexamined self beneath the surface
Key points:
1. In April 1912 the Titanic struck an iceberg; about one-ninth of an iceberg floats above the water.

3. Application: what tore the hull was the mass beneath the surface; what sinks a Christian is likewise not the storm outside.

brief21.title: Introduction: How Fear Gets In
notes: Slide text:
It doesn’t knock; it seeps under the door
Prayer grows heavy, fellowship a chore
It all starts with “a glance”
A glance at our weakness and failure
Key points:

3. It all starts with “a glance”: at our weakness, our failure, the gap between us and others.
4. Lead into Genesis 3: humanity’s first feeling was not repentance but fear.

brief21.title: Key Verse and Background
notes: Slide text:
“Lifting up their eyes, they saw no one,
except Jesus alone.”
(Matthew 17:8)
The Transfiguration: a voice from the cloud
Key points:
1. The author is Matthew the tax collector (Levi); testimony of Papias and Eusebius; written around AD 50–70 for Jewish believers.
2. Context: Peter’s confession (Matthew 16:16), then the rebuke for “setting his mind on the things of men” (Matthew 16:23).
3. Six days later, up a high mountain; Peter wanted three tents, putting the Lord on the same level as Moses and Elijah.
4. The bright cloud is the glory of God’s presence; the Father said, “This is my beloved Son … Listen to him” (Matthew 17:5).
5. The original: the “alone” in “Jesus alone” is μόνον — all the noise in their field of vision cleared away.

brief21.title: 1. The Bible’s First “Afraid”
notes: Slide text:
“I heard your voice in the garden,
and I was afraid” (Genesis 3:10)
The first “afraid” in the Bible
came when man first looked closely at himself
Key points:
1. Read Genesis 3:7–10.
2. Stress that this is the first appearance of “afraid” in the whole Bible.
3. Not at the Flood, on a battlefield or in the face of death, but the first time a human being looked closely at himself.
4. Ask: how much of our fear today also begins with “looking closely at ourselves”?

brief21.title: 1. Naked and Crafty
notes: Slide text:
Naked: arummim
The serpent’s craftiness: arum
Nothing changed but the way of seeing
Fear is reverence aimed at the wrong object
Key points:
1. Wordplay in the original: Genesis 2:25 “naked”, arummim; Genesis 3:1 the serpent’s “subtle”, arum — they sound almost the same.
2. Nakedness was once free of fear; once the serpent came in, the same nakedness became shame. Nothing changed but the way of seeing.
3. The serpent said “your eyes will be opened” (Genesis 3:5); their eyes were indeed opened, but the first thing they saw was themselves.
4. “Afraid”, yare’, can also mean “to fear” in the sense of reverence; fear is reverence aimed at the wrong object.

brief21.title: 1. Three Moves of the Self-Centred Life
notes: Slide text:
Cover: fig leaves
Hide: from the presence of Yahweh God
Shift the blame: the woman you gave me
God asks: Where are you?
Key points:
1. Three moves: cover (fig leaves), hide (from the presence of Yahweh God), shift the blame (Genesis 3:12).
2. Today’s version: covering with qualifications, job titles, busyness, even ministry; hiding in phones, work, silence.
3. Psychology: Nolen-Hoeksema’s research at Yale on “rumination” — repeatedly staring at ourselves prolongs and deepens depression.
4. God’s “Where are you?” is not because he can’t find Adam; he is asking: what position are you living in?
5. 321: pride is leaving our originally intended position, wanting to take God’s place; humility is returning to it — let man be man and let God be God.

brief21.title: 2. Looking at Self, We Can’t See the Lord
notes: Slide text:
See our lack — can’t believe his abundance
See our smallness — can’t rely on his greatness
See our weakness — can’t know his power
Focus on self brings self-pity and self-blame
Key points:
1. Read Matthew 14:28–30.
2. Three parallel lines: seeing our lack / smallness / weakness, we cannot believe in the Lord’s abundance / greatness / almighty power.
3. Focus on self = self-pity, self-blame, anxiety and fear.
4. To be fair: of the twelve, only Peter got out of the boat, and he really did walk on the water.

brief21.title: 2. Why Peter Sank
notes: Slide text:
“When he saw that the wind was strong, he was afraid”
(Matthew 14:30)
The wind didn’t change; his eyes did
Looking to Jesus: eyes taken off everything else
Key points:
1. Key word: “saw” is βλέπων, a continuing gaze, not a passing glance.
2. Main point: the wind was there all along; it didn’t get stronger — Peter’s eyes changed.
3. Compare Hebrews 12:2, “looking to”: ἀφορῶντες = taking the eyes off everything else and fixing them.

brief21.title: 2. Inattentional Blindness
notes: Slide text:
Harvard experiment: about half
missed the gorilla in the middle of the screen
Those whose attention is full of self
can’t see Jesus standing in front of them
Key points:
1. The Harvard gorilla experiment (Simons and Chabris, 1999, Perception).
2. Result: about half the participants never saw the gorilla that stayed on screen about nine seconds — “inattentional blindness”.
3. Application: when attention is full of ourselves, we become blind to Jesus right in front of us.
4. Quote: M’Cheyne (1813–1843) is generally credited with saying, “For every look at yourself, take ten looks at Christ.”
5. 321: the focus is Jesus — not ourselves, not other people, not our circumstances; Galatians 2:20, “it is no longer I who live”.

brief21.title: 3. The Ten Spies’ Report
notes: Slide text:
“We were in our own sight as grasshoppers”
(Numbers 13:33)
“And so we were in their sight”
A projection never checked
Key points:
1. Background: the twelve spies set out from Kadesh and came back after forty days with grapes and bad news (Numbers 13:27–28).
2. Verse wording: read the full verse as given in the Bible text, “We were in our own sight as grasshoppers” (Numbers 13:33).
3. “Grasshopper” is the Hebrew chagav, a little insect crushed underfoot.
4. “In their sight” was a projection out of thin air; yet Rahab said, “As soon as we had heard it, our hearts melted” (Joshua 2:11).
5. Ask: how many steps have you not dared to take because of an unchecked “people will surely see me this way”?

brief21.title: 3. Caleb and Joshua
notes: Slide text:
“Let’s go up at once, and possess it”
(Numbers 13:30)
“Yahweh is with us.
Don’t fear them” (Numbers 14:9)
Key points:
1. Caleb stilled the people (Numbers 13:30); the ten spies said, “they are stronger than we” (Numbers 13:31).
2. Caleb and Joshua said, “Yahweh is with us. Don’t fear them” (Numbers 14:9).
3. The same walls, the same sons of Anak, two opposite reports; the difference was not the intelligence but the focus.
4. The ten looked first at the giants, then at themselves, and God disappeared from view; Caleb looked first at God, and the giants became bread.

brief21.title: 3. Faith Recalibrates the Scales
notes: Slide text:
A loss hurts about twice as much as a gain pleases
(Kahneman and Tversky, 1979)
“Don’t be afraid. Don’t be dismayed”
(Joshua 1:9)
Key points:
1. Psychology: Kahneman and Tversky’s 1979 Prospect Theory in Econometrica — a loss hurts about twice as much as an equal gain pleases; Kahneman won the 2002 Nobel Prize in Economics.
2. Application: bad news always sounds twice as loud as good; the ten spies heard only the echo of the city walls.
3. Verse wording: for “Don’t be afraid … I am with you”, read the full verse, Joshua 1:9.
4. God’s assurance was not that the enemy had weakened but “I am with you”; faith is “proof of things not seen” (Hebrews 11:1).
5. Quote: Corrie ten Boom is generally credited with saying, “Worry does not empty tomorrow of its sorrow; it empties today of its strength.”

brief21.title: 4. When Is a Drop of Water Noticed?
notes: Slide text:
When it is alone, separated
Without unity, we see only ourselves
Often we are not isolated by others
but choose to separate ourselves
Key points:
1. Open with a question: when do you notice a single drop of water?
2. Answer: when it is on its own, separated, cut off from the other drops.
3. The vicious circle: looking at self → hiding → seeing self even more → more fear (Adam hiding among the trees).
4. Data: Holt-Lunstad’s 2010 meta-analysis at Brigham Young University in PLoS Medicine — 148 studies, over 300,000 people; strong social connections raised the likelihood of survival by about 50%.

brief21.title: 4. Drops and Rivers

brief21.title: 4. Glory Revealed in Unity

“That they may be one,

235: companions, parents and children, team

brief21.title: Practices 1 and 2
notes: Slide text:
Notice when you start looking at yourself
“Lord Jesus, I turn to you”
Replace fear with the language of faith
Impossible for me, possible for God
Key points:
1. Practice 1: notice the three “looking at self” sentences — I just can’t; what if it doesn’t work out; what will people think of me.
2. They look at our ability, our results and our image; when you notice them, say at once, “Lord Jesus, I turn to you.”
3. Luther is generally credited with saying: you can’t stop birds flying over your head, but you can stop them building a nest in your hair.
4. Practice 2: three declarations of faith, grounded in 2 Corinthians 12:9, Isaiah 41:10 and Matthew 19:26.
5. Eight stages: this is “Evaluation” and “Repetition”; faith comes by hearing (Romans 10:17).

brief21.title: Practice 3 and a Reminder
notes: Slide text:
Reach out and connect; refuse isolation
Greet someone, share a struggle, join a group
Reminder: feelings change, God’s word doesn’t
Let truth be greater than feelings

brief21.title: The 3-2-1 Vision in Summary

Three Foundations, Two Core Values, the Goal
Life first, then relationships, then ministry
From the human perspective to God’s
Humility overcomes pride; selflessness overcomes Satan

2. The Two Core Values: let Jesus be King, let Jesus receive all the glory; the Goal: establish God’s system.
3. Life first, then relationships, then ministry; the order of relationships: first with God, then with ourselves, then with others, last with things.

brief21.title: Closing and Call
notes: Slide text:
“Not a spirit of fear, but of power,
love, and self-control”
(2 Timothy 1:7)
Get up, don’t be afraid — lift your eyes to the Lord

4. Back to the scene: the Lord came, touched them and said, “Get up, and don’t be afraid” (Matthew 17:7).

Lord, I will no longer look at myself
I will fix my eyes on you
May I lift my eyes and see no one
except Jesus alone
Key points:
